headline: OpenAI withdraws three mathematical results from its GitHub math repo
summary: OpenAI has updated its public math repository on GitHub, including the withdrawal of three previously formalized mathematical results. This is part of an ongoing effort to maintain accuracy and expand the formalization of top-line results.
details: OpenAI has announced an update to its public GitHub math repository, which tracks the formalization of mathematical results using the Lean proof assistant. This update includes significant changes to the repo's content.

Specifically, the update features the addition of 6 new Lean formalizations and 19 modifications to existing entries. Crucially, it also includes the withdrawal of three previously published mathematical results.

With these changes, the repository now boasts approximately 42% of its top-line results formalized. OpenAI states it will continue to update the repo with further formalizations and any errata discovered.

topic: india rejects elon musk starlink discrimination claim
headline_marked: [[India rejects Elon Musk's claim]] of discrimination over Starlink launch
headline: India rejects Elon Musk's claim of discrimination over Starlink launch
summary: India's Ministry of Communications pushed back against Elon Musk's accusations, asserting its regulatory framework for satellite communications is fair and non-discriminatory as Starlink seeks to enter the market.
details: India's Ministry of Communications has rejected Elon Musk's claim that Starlink, SpaceX's satellite internet service, is being unfairly blocked from launching in the country. This rebuttal comes as Starlink continues its multi-year effort to establish commercial services in one of the world's largest internet markets.

Musk had accused unnamed "oligarchs" of obstructing Starlink's launch in India, alleging a "monopolistic chokehold" on the country's internet access. He called this alleged blocking a "crime against the people of India," claiming Starlink could provide affordable, high-speed internet to underserved populations.

The Ministry responded hours later, stating its regulatory framework is "fair and non-discriminatory" and that Starlink, along with two other licensed satellite operators, are at "broadly the same regulatory stage." All companies are currently undergoing security assessments required before they can apply for spectrum allocation.

Starlink has been working for over five years to enter India, a market with more than a billion internet subscribers. Despite securing key regulatory approvals and partnering with major telecom operators Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel last year, commercial services have yet to begin.

SpaceX has established a local team in India, led by Prabhakar Jayakumar, and has reiterated its commitment to the market. Starlink claims to have over 20 gateway sites and hundreds of antennas on the ground, adapting operations to meet India's regulatory and data-sovereignty requirements.

The company previously faced a setback in 2021 when it had to refund preorders after the Indian government flagged it for booking services without necessary licenses. Starlink also advocated for administrative spectrum allocation, a position India ultimately adopted over Reliance Jio's preference for auctions.

Notably, both Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel, Starlink's distribution partners, are also developing their own satellite internet services. Jio is collaborating with SES, while Airtel is a significant backer of Eutelsat OneWeb, another licensed satellite operator in India.

While Starlink's India launch timeline remains uncertain, the company recently launched Starlink Mobile, connecting ordinary phones to satellites, in neighboring Bangladesh. This highlights Starlink's regional expansion efforts despite the ongoing challenges in India.
